This page is generated from the help text of `quiver` on the main branch, which can be ahead of the latest release; the guides mark such commands **Next release**. Run `quiver help <command>` for the same text in your terminal.

Every command takes `-v`, `--verbose` to print more details, and `-h`, `--help`.

## quiver add

Assign skills to this project, or to every folder with --global.

A folder without .quiver.json is registered first; in a terminal it asks before, unless --yes is given. Commit the new file, so the project keeps its ID.

With --always the skills are also always-on: the assistant loads them before its first reply, from the next session on.

```sh
quiver add <id>... [flags]
```

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--always` | also make the skills always-on: loaded before the first reply |
| `--global` | change the skills served in every folder |
| `--project <string>` | project folder (default: the current folder) |
| `-y, --yes` | register a new project without asking |

**Examples**

```sh
# Assign two skills to the project in this folder
quiver add pdf anthropic/docx

# Serve a skill in every folder, and load it before the first reply
quiver add caveman --global --always

# Assign to another project folder
quiver add tdd --project ~/code/api
```

## quiver completion

Generate the autocompletion script for quiver for the specified shell. See each sub-command's help for details on how to use the generated script.

```sh
quiver completion [command]
```

## quiver delete

Delete one of your own skills from the library and commit the removal in the Quiver home, so git history still has it. It asks first.

An assigned skill is not deleted unless --force is given; then it is also unassigned everywhere. To take a skill away from one project only, use quiver remove. Skills from sources cannot be deleted one by one: quiver source remove deletes the whole source.

```sh
quiver delete <id> [flags]
```

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--force` | also unassign the skill where it is assigned |
| `-y, --yes` | do not ask for confirmation |

**Examples**

```sh
quiver delete old-draft
quiver delete release-notes --force --yes
```

## quiver doctor

Check the Quiver home, the library, the assignments and the Claude Code setup, and report each check as ok, warn or error. The last line, info, names the latest Quiver release (not with $QUIVER\_NO\_UPDATE\_CHECK).

With --fix it applies the safe fixes: it creates missing parts of the Quiver home, commits uncommitted changes in local/, deletes folders left over from an interrupted source add or remove and pin folders no pin uses, and, after asking, unassigns skills that are not in the library and deletes copies of served skills that Claude Code also loads by itself. Copies committed in git and copies in plugins are only reported.

```sh
quiver doctor [flags]
```

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--fix` | apply the safe fixes |

**Examples**

```sh
quiver doctor
quiver doctor --fix
```

## quiver edit

Open a local skill's SKILL.md in $VISUAL or $EDITOR. When the editor closes, the skill is checked and the change is committed in the Quiver home.

Skills from sources are read-only: "quiver update" would overwrite edits.

```sh
quiver edit <id> [flags]
```

**Examples**

```sh
quiver edit release-notes
```

## quiver fork

Copy a skill from a source into your own skills, so you can change it. Skills from sources are read-only, and quiver update replaces them with the upstream version.

The copy is named after the skill, or --as. Its frontmatter records where it came from (forkedFrom: \<id\>@\<commit\>). Wherever the original is assigned, globally or in a project, the copy takes its place, always-on marks included. From then on quiver edit changes what those projects get, and quiver update no longer does.

```sh
quiver fork <source/skill> [flags]
```

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--as <string>` | name of the local copy (default: the skill's name) |

**Examples**

```sh
quiver fork anthropic/pdf
quiver fork acme/review --as team-review
```

## quiver import

Move skills into the library and assign them to the project of the current folder, or to every folder.

```text
quiver import             the .claude/skills of this project (--deep: every folder of it)
quiver import <folder>    every skill in the folder and its subfolders
quiver import <skill>     one skill: its SKILL.md, its folder or a markdown file
```

A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md, or a markdown file of any name whose frontmatter has a description. Its name is the one in the frontmatter, or the folder or file name; --name sets another one when importing one skill. Markdown files without frontmatter, such as READMEs, are not skills. Skills without a description are skipped and listed at the end.

For each skill it asks where to assign it and a new name if the name is taken. --global makes every folder the default. With --yes it asks nothing: taken names are skipped.

After a skill is imported, its original is deleted, so the assistant does not load it twice; the copy in the library is committed in its git. An original committed in the git of a project is kept unless you say so, because teammates who do not use Quiver may need it; --yes keeps it too. --keep keeps every original.

```sh
quiver import [<folder> | <skill>] [flags]
```

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--deep` | without a folder: search every folder of this project, not only .claude/skills |
| `--global` | assign to every folder by default, instead of the project |
| `--keep` | keep every original |
| `--name <string>` | name in the library, when importing one skill |
| `-y, --yes` | ask nothing; delete the originals that are not committed in git |

**Examples**

```sh
# Import the .claude/skills of the project in this folder
quiver import

# Import every skill in a folder and its subfolders, and ask nothing
quiver import ~/Downloads/skill-pack --yes

# Import and keep the originals
quiver import --keep

# Import one skill under another name
quiver import ~/Downloads/greeter/SKILL.md --name demo
quiver import notes/review.md
```

## quiver init

Create the Quiver home and anything missing in it. Existing files are never overwritten.

In a terminal it then offers the rest of the setup, one step at a time; each can be skipped:

```text
1. register the MCP server with your assistants (quiver mcp install)
2. import the skills in ~/.claude/skills, for every folder
3. import the skills in the .claude/skills of the project in this folder
```

With --yes, or when not run in a terminal, it only creates the home.

```sh
quiver init [flags]
```

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-y, --yes` | ask nothing; only create the home |

**Examples**

```sh
quiver init

# Only create the home
quiver init --yes
```

## quiver list

List every skill in the library: your own (source "local") and those from sources. ASSIGNED says whether a skill is global and how many projects have it. Skills that cannot be loaded are listed as warnings at the end.

To see what one folder gets, use quiver status; for one skill, quiver where.

```sh
quiver list [flags]
```

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | print JSON |
| `--source <string>` | only skills from this source ("local" for your own skills) |
| `--unassigned` | only skills that are not assigned anywhere |

**Examples**

```sh
quiver list
quiver list --source local
quiver list --unassigned
quiver list --json
```

## quiver mcp

Run the MCP server on stdin and stdout. Assistants start this command; you do not need to run it yourself. Register it once with: quiver mcp install

The server serves the skills of the project in its working directory, or in $QUIVER\_PROJECT when that is set. It logs to ~/.quiver/logs.

```sh
quiver mcp [flags]
quiver mcp [command]
```

**Examples**

```sh
# What Claude Code runs after quiver mcp install
quiver mcp
```

## quiver mcp config

Print the mcpServers entry that starts this quiver, for an assistant that quiver mcp install does not set up. Add it to that assistant's MCP config. Nothing is changed.

```sh
quiver mcp config [flags]
```

**Examples**

```sh
quiver mcp config
```

## quiver mcp install

Register the MCP server with every supported assistant that is installed, or only with the assistants named. Some assistants use Quiver's skills only when you ask for them in the prompt; mcp install says which. For any other assistant, add the entry that quiver mcp config prints to its MCP config.

Supported assistants: claude-code, codex, cursor, claude-desktop, antigravity

Run it again after moving the quiver binary: a registration that points to another binary is replaced. In the assistants' JSON files, every other key is kept, and the old file is saved next to it with the suffix .quiver-backup.

```sh
quiver mcp install [assistant...] [flags]
```

**Examples**

```sh
quiver mcp install

# Only Cursor
quiver mcp install cursor

# Claude Code and Claude Desktop
quiver mcp install claude-code claude-desktop
```

## quiver mcp uninstall

Remove the MCP server from every supported assistant that is installed, or only from the assistants named. The Quiver home and its skills are not touched.

Supported assistants: claude-code, codex, cursor, claude-desktop, antigravity

```sh
quiver mcp uninstall [assistant...] [flags]
```

**Examples**

```sh
quiver mcp uninstall

# Only Claude Desktop
quiver mcp uninstall claude-desktop
```

## quiver new

Create a local skill in the Quiver home and assign it to this project, to every folder with --global, or nowhere with --none.

Without --description the new SKILL.md opens in $VISUAL or $EDITOR.

A folder without .quiver.json is registered first; in a terminal it asks before, unless --yes is given.

```sh
quiver new <name> [flags]
```

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--description <string>` | one sentence on when the assistant should use the skill; skips the editor |
| `--global` | change the skills served in every folder |
| `--none` | create the skill without assigning it |
| `--project <string>` | project folder (default: the current folder) |
| `-y, --yes` | register a new project without asking |

**Examples**

```sh
# Write the skill in your editor; it is served in this project
quiver new release-notes

# Create it without an editor, for every folder
quiver new commit-style --global --description "Write commit messages in our style."
```

## quiver pin

Keep a skill from a source at one commit of the source: its current commit, or the one given (a hash, tag or branch). quiver update then leaves the skill alone, so its text changes only when you decide. The pin applies everywhere the skill is assigned, and its ID stays the same.

The commit is checked out into ~/.quiver/sources/.pins. Older commits are downloaded first when the source does not have them yet. quiver unpin goes back to the source's current version. To change the skill itself, use quiver fork instead.

```sh
quiver pin <source/skill> [<commit>] [flags]
```

**Examples**

```sh
quiver pin anthropic/pdf
quiver pin acme/review 3f2a9c1
```

## quiver projects

List registered projects: name, ID, number of skills and folders. Folders that no longer exist are marked (missing).

```sh
quiver projects [flags]
quiver projects [command]
```

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | print JSON |

**Examples**

```sh
quiver projects
quiver projects --json
quiver projects rename app-k3f9q2 web
quiver projects forget old-site
```

## quiver projects forget

Remove a project and its skill assignments from the registry. The project's .quiver.json is left alone, so using the folder again registers it again with the same ID and no skills.

```sh
quiver projects forget <id|name> [flags]
```

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-y, --yes` | do not ask for confirmation |

**Examples**

```sh
quiver projects forget old-site
quiver projects forget app-k3f9q2 --yes
```

## quiver projects rename

Change the name Quiver shows for a project. The name is only a label; the project keeps its ID and skills.

```sh
quiver projects rename <id|name> <new-name> [flags]
```

**Examples**

```sh
quiver projects rename app-k3f9q2 web
quiver projects rename web web-frontend
```

## quiver projects split

Run inside a project folder that was copied with its .quiver.json. The folder gets a new ID and starts with the skills of the original; after that, changing one copy's skills does not change the other's.

```sh
quiver projects split [flags]
```

**Examples**

```sh
cp -R ~/code/app ~/code/app-v2
cd ~/code/app-v2
quiver projects split
```

## quiver remove

Unassign skills from this project, or from every folder with --global. The skills stay in the library.

With --always only the always-on mark is removed; the skills stay assigned.

```sh
quiver remove <id>... [flags]
```

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--always` | only remove the always-on mark and keep the skills assigned |
| `--global` | change the skills served in every folder |
| `--project <string>` | project folder (default: the current folder) |

**Examples**

```sh
quiver remove pdf
quiver remove caveman --global

# Keep the skill assigned, but stop loading it before the first reply
quiver remove caveman --global --always
```

## quiver search

Search the IDs, names and descriptions of every skill in the library, ignoring case. Exact names come first, then names that start with the text, then names that contain it, then descriptions. HERE says whether a skill is served in this folder: global or project.

```sh
quiver search <text> [flags]
```

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | print JSON |

**Examples**

```sh
quiver search pdf
quiver search "pull request" --json
```

## quiver show

Show a skill of the library: its ID and name, where it comes from (local, or the source and its commit), its folder, where it is assigned and whether it is always-on there, its extra files, then the text of its SKILL.md.

```sh
quiver show <id> [flags]
```

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | print JSON |

**Examples**

```sh
quiver show pdf
quiver show anthropic/docx --json
```

## quiver source

A source is a git repository with skills, such as a team's shared skills. Its skills get IDs like \<source\>/\<skill\>. They are read-only: quiver update pulls new versions.

Add only sources you trust. Their skills give instructions to your assistant and can include scripts.

```sh
quiver source [command]
```

**Examples**

```sh
quiver source add anthropics/skills --name anthropic
quiver source list
quiver source remove anthropic
```

## quiver source add

Clone a repository and add its skills to the library.

\<repo\> is owner/repo (GitHub), host/owner/repo, a git URL or a local path. The source name defaults to the repository owner.

```sh
quiver source add <repo> [flags]
```

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--name <string>` | source name (default: the repository owner) |

**Examples**

```sh
# GitHub owner/repo
quiver source add anthropics/skills --name anthropic

# Any git URL, or a local folder
quiver source add git@github.com:acme/skills.git
quiver source add ~/code/team-skills
```

## quiver source list

List the sources: name, number of skills, the commit in use and when it was made, and the repository.

```sh
quiver source list [flags]
```

**Examples**

```sh
quiver source list
```

## quiver source remove

Delete a source and its skills. It refuses while skills from the source are assigned, unless --force is given.

```sh
quiver source remove <name> [flags]
```

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--force` | unassign the source's skills first |

**Examples**

```sh
quiver source remove acme
quiver source remove acme --force
```

## quiver status

Show the project in this folder and the skills the MCP server serves here.

Like the server, it uses $QUIVER\_PROJECT instead of the current folder when it is set.

```sh
quiver status [flags]
```

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | print JSON |

**Examples**

```sh
quiver status
QUIVER_PROJECT=~/code/api quiver status
quiver status --json
```

## quiver sync

Sync the Quiver home with a git remote, so every machine has the same local skills, sources and assignments. Set it up once per machine with quiver sync init \<git-remote\>; use a private repository.

quiver sync commits the changes on this machine, pulls the others with rebase and pushes. When registry.json or config.json changed on both machines, the changes are merged: a skill assigned on either machine stays assigned. Any other conflict stops the sync with nothing pulled or pushed, and says how to resolve it. Sources added on another machine are cloned afterwards.

Only local/, config.json and registry.json are synced. sources/ is cloned again from config.json, and the folders where each project was seen stay on each machine.

```sh
quiver sync [flags]
quiver sync [command]
```

**Examples**

```sh
quiver sync init git@github.com:me/quiver-home.git
quiver sync
```

## quiver sync init

Turn the Quiver home into a git repository with \<git-remote\> as its remote, and push it. The history of local/ is kept; local/ stops being a repository of its own.

Run it on every machine with the same remote. When the remote already holds another machine's home, this machine's skills, sources and assignments are merged with it. If the same local skill differs on both, it stops and changes nothing.

```sh
quiver sync init <git-remote> [flags]
```

**Examples**

```sh
quiver sync init git@github.com:me/quiver-home.git
```

## quiver unpin

Remove the pin of a source skill, so it is served from the source's current version again and quiver update changes it as usual.

```sh
quiver unpin <source/skill> [flags]
```

**Examples**

```sh
quiver unpin anthropic/pdf
```

## quiver update

Pull the latest skills of the given sources, or of every source. For each source it first downloads the new commits without applying them, and lists the skills that would be added, changed or removed. For each assigned skill that changes, it lists the changed files, and marks scripts (such as .sh, .py and .js files, and executable files) as "needs review": the assistant may run them. --diff shows the whole change of those skills.

When an assigned skill would change or go away, it asks before it applies the changes; --yes applies them without asking. Changes to skills that are not assigned are applied right away. Pinned skills are left alone.

A source whose history was rewritten (force-pushed) is not updated; run again with --reset to take the remote history.

```sh
quiver update [<name>...] [flags]
```

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--diff` | show the whole change of each assigned skill that changes |
| `--reset` | replace a rewritten history (after a force-push) with the remote one |
| `-y, --yes` | apply the changes without asking |

**Examples**

```sh
quiver update
quiver update anthropic --diff
quiver update --yes
quiver update acme --reset
```

## quiver where

Show where a skill is assigned: "global" if it is served in every folder, then each project that has it, with its folders.

```sh
quiver where <id> [flags]
```

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | print JSON |

**Examples**

```sh
quiver where pdf
quiver where anthropic/docx --json
```
